Root.loopFocus.semantic: keyboard navigation wraps to the other end of the toolbar once the end is reached.

Root.orientation.semantic: toolbar orientation; selects the roving-focus arrow axis.

Root.disabled.semantic: no @default documented; disables the toolbar (data-disabled on Root/Group/Button/Input).

Button.disabled / focusableWhenDisabled.semantic: a disabled toolbar button stays focusable by default (APG toolbar pattern) and exposes data-focusable; keyboard events other than Tab are prevented while disabled.

Input.disabled / focusableWhenDisabled /.semantic: native <input> that participates in toolbar keyboard navigation; disable focusableWhenDisabled to remove it from the roving order.

Button composition.semantic: documented integration: pass any Base UI popup trigger to <Toolbar.Button render={<Menu.Trigger/>}> (the docs demo uses render={<Toggle/>} and render={<Select.Trigger/>}); for Tooltip the toolbar item goes into <Tooltip.Trigger render={<Toolbar.Button/>}>. NumberField integrates via <Toolbar.Input render={<NumberField.Input/>}>.

Group / Separator / Link.type: Group renders <div>; Separator renders <div>; Link renders <a>
Group / Separator / Link.semantic: Group has no props beyond BaseUIComponentProps (use aria-label for its accessible name); Separator/Link are presentational; every part accepts render/className/style.

Toolbar.Root.ItemMetadata.semantic: metadata the toolbar tracks per registered item (exposed as a type for consumers composing custom items).

dataAttributes: Button: data-disabled, data-orientation, data-focusable (remains focusable while disabled)
renderProp: Toolbar is the canonical `render`-based composition surface: `<Toolbar.Button render={<Toggle/>}/>` (docs demo), `<Toolbar.Button render={<Select.Trigger/>}/>`, `<Toolbar.Input render={<NumberField.Input/>}/>`, and the reverse direction `<Tooltip.Trigger render={<Toolbar.Button/>}/>`. Standard contract: render?: ReactElement | (props, state) => ReactElement, plus state-driven className/style. Custom primitives: useRender; merging: mergeProps/mergePropsN (handlers merged right-to-left, className concatenated, style merged, ref NOT merged).
controlled: None — Toolbar has no value/open state (no controlled props, no default props, no change callbacks). State belongs to the composed controls (ToggleGroup/Select/Menu/etc.) or to the consumer.
formIntegration: None. `Toolbar.Input` is a plain native input for filtering/editing inside the toolbar; there is no name/value submission wrapper, hidden input or validation state (Field.Root data-* are not emitted by Toolbar parts).
keyboard: Roving focus between toolbar items along the toolbar's orientation (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight when horizontal, ArrowUp/ArrowDown when vertical — handled by the shared composite internals that Toolbar consumes, with key constants ARROW_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT + Home/End in internals/composite/composite.mjs); `loopFocus` (default true) wraps focus at the ends. Disabled items stay in the tab/focus order when `focusableWhenDisabled` is true (default) and swallow keys other than Tab (useFocusableWhenDisabled.mjs), otherwise they are removed from navigation. Tab moves focus out of the toolbar. No typeahead, no PageUp/PageDown.
notableDifferences: React Aria's toolbar lives in `react-aria-components`' Toolbar (with ToggleButtonGroup/Button/Link/Separator); Base UI's Toolbar adds `Toolbar.Input` (with NumberField integration) and a `focusableWhenDisabled` prop that defaults to TRUE — a straight prop rename from React Aria's Toolbar will change disabled-item focusability if you do not set it.

Item composition is explicit via `render` (Button renders Toggle/Select.Trigger/Menu.Trigger) rather than React Aria's context-based ToolbarItem composition; the Tooltip integration direction is inverted (item into Tooltip.Trigger's render).

State attributes are only data-orientation/data-disabled/data-focusable — there is no data-selected/data-pressed on toolbar parts (pressed state comes from the composed Toggle, e.g. data-pressed in the docs demo).
`Toolbar.Group` and `Toolbar.Separator` take their accessible names/orientation from context (aria-label on the Group).
